source_node.label: piSignage Arbitrary File Read via Path Traversal
source_node.precondition: Remote network access and authenticated low-privilege account on piSignage player API (version < 2.6.4)
source_node.postcondition: Download and disclosure of arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi filesystem (e.g., system configs, shadow hashes, application secrets)

target_node.label: RaspAP Authenticated Web Console Command Execution
target_node.precondition: Authenticated access to RaspAP 2.5 web interface (obtained via default/cracked credentials or file disclosure)
target_node.postcondition: Arbitrary OS command execution, file upload, and underlying host code execution on the Raspberry Pi

source_evidence.description: The web application component of piSignage before 2.6.4 allows a remote attacker (authenticated as a low-privilege user) to download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal. In other words, this issue is in the player API for log download.

An issue was discovered in includes/webconsole.php in RaspAP 2.5. With authenticated access, an attacker can use a misconfigured (and virtually unrestricted) web console to attack the underlying OS (Raspberry Pi) running this software, and execute commands on the system (including ones for uploading of files and execution of code).

source_node.precondition: Target victim accesses a malicious remote web page using Oculus Browser (versions 5.2.7 to 5.7.11)
source_node.postcondition: Arbitrary HTML injection in browser UI, UI spoofing, and potential client-side code execution in user context

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Hardlink Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Local unprivileged execution rights on Windows system running Oculus Desktop (< 1.44.0.32849)
target_node.postcondition: Arbitrary file write with privileged permissions via hard link to log file, resulting in SYSTEM-level privilege escalation

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Writing to an unprivileged file from a privileged OVRRedir.exe process in Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file.
